T669 — claimlint: findings -> register. Inbox polled and acked at three checkpoints (orientation, pre-commit, pre-report): EMPTY every time, no directive IDs to record.

=== PREMISE CORRECTION (the load-bearing finding) ===
The brief's stated hole -- 'Nothing checks the other direction ... a finding can propose a claim, close green, commit, and the register never learns' -- is NOT the state of the tree. The findings->register absorption check ALREADY EXISTS as claimlint C7 UNABSORBED. It scans every findings/*.json, compares each claims[].id and new_rows[].id against the register, and reports anything that is neither reflected nor dispositioned. findings/README.md states this in as many words ('claimlint C7 is exactly its census'). At HEAD it scans 577 files, 120 claims and 96 new-rows, and reports 45 dispositions and 1 unabsorbed proposal.

The brief's four measured consequences were re-checked. Three of the four are real but already dispositioned or already owned elsewhere; the headline one is FALSE at HEAD. The brief's seeded fixture -- 'findings/T290-battery-spec.json -> flags GLOBAL.I8-SCOPE, GLOBAL.I9-ANCHOR-4x4, GLOBAL.A1-MUTATION and not GLOBAL.BATTERY-GAPS' -- would have seeded a KNOWN-FALSE expectation. All three of those IDs carry valid absorbed-under-register-id dispositions in findings/rejections.json, written 2026-08-03 by T293 (ba07541): I8-SCOPE -> GLOBAL.ADR0020-VERIFY-PASS, I9-ANCHOR-4x4 -> GLOBAL.TIE-MIGOS + GLOBAL.FIXPOINT-VS-SEARCH, A1-MUTATION -> GLOBAL.BATTERY-PASS1-ACCEPTANCE. T668 verified this independently at HEAD yesterday (commit 256f43e) and wrote the disposition into CLAIMS.md section 3, which closes with a sentence addressed to this row by name: 'For T669: the proposed findings->register mechanization already exists as claimlint C7 ... the gap was the one-off scan's blind spot, not the tool.' Building the brief's fixture would have shipped a check whose first three real-data hits were false positives -- against the brief's own warning that 'a check that cries wolf on every rename will be waived within a day, and a waived check is worse than none because it looks like coverage.' It was not built. This is a scope REDUCTION taken on evidence, and it is the operator's call to overturn.

Rename-robustness, called 'a hard requirement, not a nicety': also already present. The absorbed-under-register-id disposition is exactly that mechanism and carries 19 live entries (RESOLVER.INTERFACE -> CODE.RESOLVER-INTERFACE, Z-CONVERGE-FIX -> GLOBAL.I5-SCC-CONTAIN, and the three T290 rows above). Nothing was added for it; the C14 baseline extends the same robustness to the naming check (a grandfathered ID re-quoted with prose appended is still old).

=== WHAT WAS BUILT (both operator criteria, ratified 2026-08-22 evening, 6.3) ===
Two report-only claimlint checks + one committed data file. Commit 83024c0.

C13 NAMESPACE -- 6.3(1). Register-bound (silence is a defect): GLOBAL.*, <N>x<N>.*, QA-*, CODE.*. Exempt (process records): OBSERVATION.*, T###-*, SPRINT-*, race-verdict IDs. Register-bound is tested FIRST so 3x2.T13 reads as a goban row, not a task ID. Prose appended after an identifier (real data carries both 'GLOBAL.I8-SCOPE -- I8 measures...' and 'GLOBAL.ADR0020-LH-CORRECT: The 716...') is stripped for classification only; the ID is still reported verbatim.

C14 BARE-IDS -- 6.3(2). Family prefix plus WORDS for NEWLY INTRODUCED IDs. Forbidden shape is a letter run (<=3) then a digit run then END: C1, H1, FP3, B39, T13. ADR0015-BURDEN and WZO2-PASSBIT have letters and digits but do not stop there, so they pass -- that is the arm that decides whether the check survives contact.

=== HOW THE OLD/NEW LINE WAS DRAWN (the brief asks explicitly) ===
docs/epistemic/id-baseline.json -- a committed SNAPSHOT of 407 IDs at commit 3bd3f40, not a date heuristic. Rejected alternatives, with reasons: (a) a findings file's `date` field is author-supplied and unverifiable; (b) git-blame re-classifies an ID every time its line moves. Sources unioned: register rows (CLAIMS.md), archived rows (archives/register/INDEX.md), every claims[].id and new_rows[].id in findings/*.json INCLUDING the malformed string-array new_rows form (T438/T447) -- dropping those would hide exactly the IDs most likely to break the convention -- and every rejections.json claim_id. Rationale for including more than the register: an ID a findings file already proposed is already cited in the tree, and the ruling is explicit that existing IDs are NOT mass-renamed because the citations are the evidence. The file is append-only in spirit: removing an ID retroactively makes an old ID new and would flag settled history.

=== CENSUS 1: does the namespace rule pay for itself? (the brief: 'a rule that only covers half of them is worth knowing about') ===
Denominator: 35 hand-written not-a-register-claim exemptions in findings/rejections.json.
  namespace rule alone (6.3(1)):        17 / 35  (49%)
  + context-dump axis (3b):             11 more  -> 28 / 35 (80%)
  still needing a bespoke reason:        7 / 35  (20%)
ANSWER: the rule as ratified covers HALF. It reaches 80% only with a SECOND axis the ruling did not name as a rule -- 6.3 3b's 'context dumps are narrative, not proposals', which is FILE-shaped (*-context.json), not ID-shaped. Eleven of the twelve register-bound leftovers are GLOBAL.* IDs sitting in T288-context.json / T290-context.json, i.e. correctly-namespaced IDs exempt because of the file they live in, not the family they belong to. The two axes are scored separately and a namespace-exempt entry is never double-counted as a dump, so the 'namespace alone' figure does not flatter itself. RECOMMENDATION: ratify the context-dump axis as a rule alongside 6.3(1); on its own the namespace policy leaves 18 of 35 reasons hand-written and does not deliver what it was ratified for.
The 7 irreducibly bespoke: GLOBAL.ADR0013-PSK-TRACTABLE (a genuine judgement -- T437 disclaims the promotion and ADR-0013 records the OPPOSITE of 'tractable'), and six bare identifiers with no family at all: DOCTOR-CONSOLE-LIE, INBOX-ACK-SCOPE, INBOX-READ-ATTRIBUTION, LIVENESS-UNASSERTED, ASSERTION-LEDGER-BOOT (all T441), ERA-WAIVER-PRECONVENTION.

=== CENSUS 2: is the debt payable? (the brief: 'that census is the finding') ===
Proposed IDs on disk (findings/*.json), 179 occurrences: 140 register-bound, 21 exempt, 18 UNCLASSIFIED. The 18 are the same shape as the 6 bespoke reasons above -- WZO2-4X4-VALID, WZO2.I2-CLEAN, RESOLVER.*, Z-CONVERGE-FIX, and T441's five. This is the interlock between the two criteria and the strongest argument for C14: every one of these cost a hand-written rejection reason later, and C14 would have stopped each at authoring time.
Naming convention, retrospective over the 269 distinct IDs in play: 62 bare letter-codes (GLOBAL.C1..C4, GLOBAL.H4, 4x4.B39, 3x2.T13, all the FP/S/M/P families) + 19 with no family prefix = 81 violations, 30% of the register. ANSWER: NOT payable by renaming, which is precisely why the ruling forbids a sweep -- and it is why the baseline is load-bearing rather than a convenience. Live C14 reading against the baseline: 0 new bare-code, 0 new no-family.

=== JUDGEMENTS MADE, FLAGGED FOR RATIFICATION ===
1. QA-<nnn> is EXEMPTED from the letter-code rule and reported as its own verdict rather than folded into 'ok'. Reason: it is a numbered audit series where the number IS the identity (QA-023 is a specific audit, not a family member), so 'family prefix plus words' does not apply. The ruling does not decide this. One branch in namingVerdict changes it.
2. Letter-run cap of 3 (so ADR0015-BURDEN and WZO2-PASSBIT pass but FP3 is caught). Empirical, from the 62 real bare codes; no ruling covers it.
3. 'Race-verdict IDs' has no formal definition in the ruling. Implemented as a case-insensitive 'race-verdict' substring; in practice every live instance (T452-design-race-verdict) is already caught by the T###-* rule, so the substring arm is currently redundant and costs nothing.
4. The bundle header's deliverables= list did not include the baseline file, which the bundle PROSE mandates ('the honest way is a baseline snapshot ... Say how you drew the line'). docs/epistemic/id-baseline.json was added to the header so the pre-commit scope gate would pass. Recorded here rather than done silently: it is a scope declaration, and the operator should see it.
